entities.summary:
Regnaud de La Porte (also known as Raynaud or Reynaud), a prominent French cardinal and statesman, played a crucial role in the ecclesiastical and political landscape of early 14th-century Europe, particularly during the nascent years of the Avignon Papacy. Born in Allassac, Limousin, his career spanned from a distinguished jurist and bishop in France to a cardinal-priest in the Roman Curia, serving under Popes Clement V and John XXII. His influence extended through key diplomatic missions and administrative reforms, contributing to the consolidation of papal authority and the restructuring of the Church's financial and legal systems in a period of significant transition.

De La Porte commenced his ecclesiastical ascent as Bishop of Limoges in 1294, a position he held for over two decades, where he was noted for his administrative acumen and legal expertise. His appointment as Archbishop of Bourges in 1316 further elevated his standing, granting him metropolitan authority over a vast ecclesiastical province. In 1318, Pope John XXII, recognizing his capabilities, elevated him to the cardinalate, assigning him the title of Santi Nereo e Achilleo. As a cardinal, he became a trusted advisor, participating in important consistories and contributing to the legal and theological debates that shaped the Church's response to contemporary challenges, including the suppression of the Knights Templar and the burgeoning Franciscan controversies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Regnaud de La Porte was a key figure in the administrative and diplomatic machinery of the early Avignon Papacy, contributing significantly to the consolidation of papal authority and the development of canon law. His career reflected the broader shift of papal power and influence towards France in the early 14th century.
